br01.gold_connection: Refund requests clustering within 48 hours of a promo code launch are card-testing rings validating stolen cards, so the refund queue is the earliest fraud detector the store has.
br01.gold_implication: Flag refunds requested within 48 hours on orders whose payment method is under 7 days old, then compare that set against chargebacks arriving 30 to 60 days later.
br01.hidden_mechanism: refund spikes right after promo launches are card-testing validation runs

br02.gold_connection: Showing an evaluator the previous score anchors the new one upward, whether the evaluator is an LLM judge re-scoring an iteration or a grant panel scoring a resubmission.
br02.gold_implication: Re-run the internal grant self-scoring rubric with prior scores hidden and compare against the anchored version.
br02.hidden_mechanism: anchoring on previously visible scores inflates both LLM judges and grant reviewers

br03.gold_connection: Adherence to a fixed-window protocol and packet delivery to a fixed-window gateway fail the same way: the sender's schedule jitters while the receiver's window does not move.
br03.gold_implication: Switch dose reminders from "hours since last dose" to a fixed clock time for two weeks and measure adherence against the previous two weeks.
br03.hidden_mechanism: a fixed listen window on the receiving side requires a fixed emit schedule on the sending side

br04.gold_connection: An A/B lift measured on the same week the variant was tuned on is a leaked estimate; the honest number comes from the period after tuning, a temporal holdout.
br04.gold_implication: Recompute the landing variant's lift using only the week after tuning ended.
br04.hidden_mechanism: evaluating on the tuning window is leakage; use the following period as a temporal holdout

br05.gold_connection: Sequential identifiers across accounts or companies that claim to be independent expose one operator, whether the identifiers are phone numbers in a fraud ring or company registration numbers in duplicate grant applications.
br05.gold_implication: Run a sequential-identifier scan over new signups' phone numbers and over applicant company registration numbers.
br05.hidden_mechanism: sequential identifiers across supposedly independent entities reveal a single operator

br06.gold_connection: A felt improvement after starting a supplement while also starting to track sleep has no baseline; the tracking can be the effect, exactly like a personalised system beating nothing but matching the no-data control.
br06.gold_implication: Run two weeks with the ring but without the supplement, then compare against the two weeks on the supplement.
br06.hidden_mechanism: without a no-intervention baseline the measured effect may be the measurement itself

br07.gold_connection: A flash-sale email hitting the whole list at once is a thundering herd on checkout, the same failure as 200 sensors reporting together after a power restore; randomised staggering fixes both.
br07.gold_implication: Split the next campaign send into 10 batches over 30 minutes and compare checkout error rate against the last single-blast send.
br07.hidden_mechanism: thundering herd; stagger the senders with randomised backoff

br08.gold_connection: Grant KPIs should be emitted as continuous events with daily rollups, like sensor telemetry, because reconstructing them from raw history at quarter end fails once the underlying logs are gone.
br08.gold_implication: Add a KPI event log this week that appends one line per milestone event and a daily rollup.
br08.hidden_mechanism: emit progress as continuous telemetry with rollups instead of reconstructing at reporting time

br09.gold_connection: A dose schedule needs a per-window velocity rule with a hold, the way card transactions are rate-limited per ten minutes, because a total weekly cap does not stop doubling up after a missed day.
br09.gold_implication: Add a rule of at most one dose per 20-hour window to the tracker and count how often it would have fired in the last month.
br09.hidden_mechanism: rate-limit per window with a hold, not just a total cap

br10.gold_connection: Subscription churn peaking at cycle three and protocol dropout peaking at week three are the same expectation-lag failure: results lag the effort, so people quit right before they would have seen them.
br10.gold_implication: Send a "what to expect by week three" message on day 10 and measure cycle-three churn against the previous cohort.
br10.hidden_mechanism: expectation-lag dropout at the third cycle; intervene before it with a timeline

br11.gold_connection: An LLM judge drifts silently like a temperature sensor, so it needs the same treatment: a fixed reference set re-scored on a schedule, with an alert when the mean moves.
br11.gold_implication: Build a 50-item reference set, re-score it weekly with the judge, and alert if the mean shifts more than two percent.
br11.hidden_mechanism: a reference set re-scored on a schedule detects silent judge drift, like sensor calibration

br12.gold_connection: Both funnels waste the expensive step on people who fail a cheap screen afterwards: grant applications rejected on eligibility after weeks of writing, and protocol purchases refunded after a contraindication check; the screen belongs before the expensive step.
br12.gold_implication: Put a five-question eligibility check in front of the grant intake form and measure how many applicants it turns away.
br12.hidden_mechanism: move the cheap eligibility screen ahead of the expensive step in the funnel
